correctness.rationale: All constructors of lax-split PL(NE) are handled in the reconstructed small-subteam induction. Union closure of a nonempty finite family defines a maximum conclusion-model. If a small premise model lies below it, convexity transfers conclusion truth to any intermediate model; otherwise adjoining one missing valuation preserves antecedent by convexity and refutes conclusion by maximality. Empty/unsatisfiable and zero-occurrence edge cases are separated. Explicit characteristic-valuation formulas prove the bound m+1 is sharp for each m. Polynomial certificates with P model checking prove coNP containment; classical tautology yields hardness. The bundled semantic checker confirms finite instances without being used as an infinite proof.

Broader complexity results for all team logics would not automatically imply the exact coNP result for this language.

value.rationale: The motivating 2025 paper explicitly raises the exact complexity of semantic entailment as future work. The finding supplies a tight m+1 certificate for *all* finite instances and an exact coNP-completeness theorem. It explains structurally why model compression can preserve failure of a non-monotone conclusion, which the source small-model theorem did not address. Sharpness for every m rules out an artifact of small finite enumeration.
